Branson Board approves $29.1 million contract for 76 Country Boulevard project
Branson's Board has approved a $29.1 million contract for major upgrades along West 76 Country Boulevard beginning later this month. The project focuses on improving walkability while maintaining business access throughout phased construction.
A major transformation of Branson’s 76 Country Boulevard is set to begin after the Board of Aldermen approved a $29.1 million construction contract with Hartman & Company, Inc., according to an Oct. 14 announcement from city officials. The project, a collaboration between the City of Branson and the 76 Entertainment Community Enhancement District (76ECID), is scheduled to start on October 26 and follows years of planning and investment.
Mayor Larry Milton said, “The heart of Branson’s entertainment industry is critical to our community and our economy. Progress on this project has been a long time coming, and the restart of construction is a milestone worth celebrating. We are investing in the businesses, people and experiences that make Branson special while strengthening this iconic corridor for the future.”
The Streetscape Project aims to improve walkability along the boulevard by upgrading sidewalks and pedestrian crossings, installing new roadway and drainage systems, burying utilities, updating pavement markings and signage, as well as enhancing water lines for better service and fire flow capacities. Construction will extend from Shepherd of the Hills Expressway toward the Branson Ferris Wheel over an expected period of 20 months.
Chuck O’Day, chairman of the 76ECID Board of Directors, said, “The private businesses who formed the 76ECID should be commended for their desire and determination to reinvest in the economic hub of tourism for our region. Together, the private sector and the City of Branson are making this project a reality to help ensure the long-term success of our destination.”
Construction will take place in phases to minimize disruptions along this busy area. Motorists can expect temporary lane closures or traffic shifts during different stages; however, full roadway closures are not anticipated. The contract includes requirements that access be maintained for businesses throughout each phase.
Hartman & Company was selected through a competitive bidding process based on its experience with transportation projects in southwest Missouri, including highway improvements in Springfield and intersection upgrades in Christian County. Updates regarding construction phases and traffic impacts will be shared with residents, businesses, and visitors as work progresses.
